name: Venezuela
summary: A republic on the Caribbean coast of South America, separate from Gran Colombia since 1830, birthplace of Simón Bolívar and home to the world’s largest proven oil reserves.

knownFor.label: El Sistema
knownFor.note: A free youth orchestra programme copied worldwide.

location.value: Northern South America on the Caribbean; about 916,000 km².

terrain.value: Andes in the west, the Llanos plains, the Orinoco River and the Guiana Highlands.

climate.value: Tropical, with a hot and humid coast, cooler Andes highlands and a wet and dry season.

resources.value: Oil (largest proven reserves), gold, iron, farmland.

disasters.value: The Vargas mudslides of December 1999 killed thousands of people on the coast.

urbanisation.value: Caracas, the capital, Maracaibo and Valencia are the main cities, and most people live in cities.

disease.value: Malaria returned during the economic crisis.

migration.value: About 7–8 million people have left since 2015.

economicBase.value: Oil exports dominate the economy, as they have since the 1920s.

tradeRoutes.value: Oil exports to the US, later China and others.

wealth.value: Rich in the 1970s; severe crisis since 2014.

moneyAndTax.value: The bolívar; hyperinflation in 2016–21 wiped out its value and led to several redenominations.

inequality.value: Very high inequality, which grew with the economic collapse of the 2010s.

governmentType.value: A presidential republic; long periods of military rule.

keyRulers.value: José Antonio Páez (first president, 1830); Hugo Chávez (elected 1998).
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Venezuela (checked 8 Nov 2026); Country Studies: Venezuela, century of caudillismo (checked 15 Nov 2026) (Páez ruled about 1830–46; the page does not cover Chávez or the 1830 split from Gran Colombia, and dates the Federal War 1858–63 where the entry says 1859–63)

succession.value: Elections have been repeatedly disputed, with accusations of unfairness and fraud.

institutions.value: Institutions such as the courts and electoral council have been weakened since the 2000s.

stability.value: Civil wars in the 19th century; coup attempts (1992); political crisis since 2013.

armyAndTech.value: The armed forces are closely tied to politics and the state, with a role in the economy.

territoryChange.value: Disputes with Guyana over the Essequibo region and with Colombia over the Gulf of Venezuela.

alliancesRivals.value: Strengthened ties with Russia, China, Iran, Cuba, Turkey and others.

inventions.value: No major inventions are recorded; the El Sistema youth orchestra programme (1975) is a well-known cultural export.

openness.value: Varied: open to oil trade and migration at times, restricted by controls and sanctions at others.

religion.value: Mostly Catholic, with a growing Evangelical minority.

languageWriting.value: Spanish; the constitution also recognises more than thirty Indigenous languages, such as Wayuu, Warao and Pemón.

artsArchitecture.value: Joropo music, the El Sistema orchestras, painting by Armando Reverón and the Ciudad Universitaria in Caracas.

socialStructure.value: A mixed-race (mestizo) majority, with Indigenous and Afro-Venezuelan communities.

sharedIdentity.value: Simón Bolívar, the Liberator, is the central national symbol.

dailyLife.value: City apartments and hillside barrios; arepas, black beans, plantain.

ideasReligions.value: The Bolivarian Revolution, which began after Hugo Chávez was elected in 1998.

colonisation.value: A former Spanish colony, part of the Spanish Empire until independence in 1821.

riseSignals.value: Left Gran Colombia in 1830 after a rebellion led by José Antonio Páez.

peakPeriod.value: The oil boom of the 1970s, when oil income rose sharply.

declineSignals.value: Economic collapse after 2014, as oil prices fell and output dropped.
